gateway.text:
Both approaches aim to help T cells recognize cancer, but they do it at different points.

**Personalized cancer vaccine:** it supplies selected tumor material—often based on tumor-specific mutations—to **train and expand the person’s existing T cells**. The T cell still uses its natural **T-cell receptor (TCR)**, which recognizes a tumor-derived peptide only when it is displayed by the right **HLA** molecule. Therefore, target selection asks: Is the mutation truly in the tumor, expressed, processed into a peptide, displayed, and recognizable? [Vaccine overview](/education/guides/personalized-cancer-vaccine/index/#the-big-ideas) [Read tumor and normal data](/education/guides/personalized-cancer-vaccine/02-reading-tumor-and-normal-data/)

**Engineered cell therapy:** it changes the T cell by giving it a selected receptor. A **CAR** usually recognizes an accessible molecule directly on the tumor-cell surface; an engineered **TCR** recognizes a peptide–HLA pair. Target selection emphasizes enough tumor recognition while limiting recognition of healthy tissue, including checking the exact epitope and possible cross-reactivity. [Engineered-cell overview](/education/guides/engineered-cell-therapy/index/#the-big-ideas) [Choosing a target](/education/guides/engineered-cell-therapy/02-choosing-a-target/)

**Analogy:** a vaccine teaches existing scouts what clues to look for; engineered therapy equips the scouts with a new detection device.

Would you like a simple side-by-side diagram of **vaccine vs CAR-T vs TCR-T**?
